adventure.title: The Witch of Blackbriar Hall
adventure.synopsis: Blackbriar Vale remembers Judith Crowl by what arrived when no one else would send it: grain during the famine, beds during the pox, burial money when a household could not pay. Fifteen years later, each kindness has a receipt. Judith selects the vale's witches, removes their children, stores inconvenient dead, and keeps every household close enough to answer her knock. She bought that power through three chosen betrayals: nineteen refugees barred inside a burning granary for the Guest in Ash, thirty-one plague dead erased in quicklime for the Worm in White, and stolen children's names lowered into Moonless Mere for the Child Behind Glass. Canon Ysra's examiners were already approaching when Mara Sedge linked seven false prosecutions and Nell Sedge mapped the mirror dormitory. Judith took Nell, moved Mara's burning before the customary answer-night, and turned the annual Renewal of Mercy into the Hollow Feast. At first light she places the torch in eleven-year-old Tomas Sedge's hands. By midnight, the Mercy Book, household carriers, and four controlled living voices can join every door still answering Judith's claim. The commissioned company must keep the Sedge family alive, find the people and records Judith has moved, expose the roads behind her apparent omniscience, complete the material obligations she inverted, and break a feast built to continue after its hostess dies.
adventure.premise: Canon Ysra Vale sent your company to compare burial fees with parish graves and inspect Saint Mercy House after two letters went unanswered. Before dawn, Brother Caldus's rider finds you on the road with a sharper report: Nell Sedge vanished three nights ago, Mara Sedge named Judith Crowl as the taker, and the reeve has advanced Mara's execution before the customary answer-night. You reach Saint Orra's Gallows as Judith orders Mara's eleven-year-old son to light the pyre. The death roll has been cut and rebound. The reeve hides a blackthorn token. Every household owes Judith a sack, cure, bed, burial, or life. Canon Ysra's seal can hold Mara alive, preserve evidence, and protect immediate witnesses; it cannot govern the vale for you. The Renewal of Mercy begins before dusk. At midnight Judith means to turn the vale's separate debts into the Unwelcome Court's common invitation.
adventure.explanation:
Judith Crowl is the witch. Fifteen years ago she sought the Unwelcome Court because affection could be withdrawn, while debt could be recorded, inherited, and enforced. She chose each bargain, renewed it when it weakened, and built ordinary relief work around the access it purchased.

The Guest in Ash was her first account. During the famine, Judith entered nineteen road families on Saint Vey's refuge roll, took their labor on the granary roof, barred the doors on the third night, and welcomed the Guest across the threshold they trusted. The fire burned inward. The Guest now carries her across marked hearths, turns domestic flame against a household, closes claimed exits, and folds passage into soot. Her private ledger still records all nineteen as safely discharged.

The Worm in White followed during the pox. Families paid Judith to carry thirty-one bodies to honest ground. She cut off the tags, laid the dead in quicklime beneath the orchard, and denied each body a final witness. The Worm moves sickness, works abandoned flesh, spoils stores, and lays Judith's wounds on the unburied. Later patients whose suffering inconvenienced her accounts became renewal bodies.

The Child Behind Glass came with Saint Mercy House. Judith records children under their whole names, copies chosen names onto silvered slips, and lowers the vessels into Moonless Mere. The Child lends voices, dreams, false recognition, written command, and reflected roads. It named the price before Judith paid it; she returned with more names and built forms, dormitories, transfers, and receiving beds into a steady acquisition system. Saint Mercy House is not an independent good she later corrupted. Judith made the care effective because every cured fever, occupied bed, and winter meal placed another person inside a room, record, or obligation she could inventory.

Judith also manufactures the witches she condemns. Petition paper becomes a planted poppet. An illness moves into a household. The dependent most likely to be believed disappears. Ordinary officers receive enough fear or favor to finish the accusation, and Judith offers the survivors grain, medicine, custody, or protection. Tokens, receipts, copied names, and stolen hearth ash extend a network that crows, servants, mirrors, wagons, and marked people must physically carry. Her knowledge is formidable because the network is busy, finite, and well supplied.

That distributed system kept any one failure from exposing the whole. It also ended when Caldus's duplicate burial figures reached Canon Ysra, Mara connected seven prosecutions, and Nell mapped the mirror dormitory. Judith's couriers learned when the examiners would arrive. She took Nell, framed Mara, advanced the burning, and rewrote the Renewal of Mercy as a final consolidation. Slow ownership is about to become public evidence.

Forty-seven households display a blackthorn token. Eleven more have signed the Mercy Book. Five have done neither. Judith means the reeve's Renewal oath to answer for the vale and catch the unmarked doors, but an explicit household refusal blocks a new connection and can turn an existing copied door outward once its material carriers are revoked. The Mercy Book names hosts. Tokens and stolen ash carry household claims. Seven silvered names prepare the choir bays and coordinate the Glass Nurse, but a vessel is not a voice: at least four living, controlled speakers must stand in the Underhall. The Hollow Feast operates while any two of three components—the Mercy Book, token network, and captive choir—remain joined. Midnight reaches only the doors still connected.

Ysra's writ authorizes record inspection, evidence preservation, a temporary stay of an unlawful execution, and immediate witness protection. It grants no permanent rule, general command over the reeve's guards, title to Blackbriar property, or power to dispose of victims without their families and witnesses. Later operations rest on discovered unlawful custody, immediate rescue, ordinary defense, willing household or parish cooperation, and narrow public orders from local officers who accept responsibility. Government, property settlement, and final judgment wait for outside civil and chapel authorities.

Each pact ends only when living people complete the obligation Judith inverted. Open the Burned Refuge without welcoming the Guest, restore the nineteen names, and burn the lying shelter ledger in a hearth freely offered by someone Judith betrayed. Identify the pit-dead, lift them safely from quicklime, and give them burial or burning beneath a bell that states where they were found and who denied them. Speak each stolen name back in an unborrowed reflection before breaking its vessel. Doors, records, bodies, witnesses, transport, care, and final disposition are the rite.

Two severed pacts make Judith's body mortal. Three prevent the Court from taking up her claim cleanly. Killing her may be necessary, but the common welcome can outlive her through the Mercy Book, household tokens, and captive choir. Removing any two components collapses the valley-wide claim. Unrevoked household carriers may still support smaller claims afterward.

Keep Judith in the work. At the gallows she makes Tomas hold the torch. At Saint Mercy House she names the meals, medicines, bottles, and receiving beds a rescue will require. At Blackbriar Hall she offers exact benefits whose costs she has assigned to someone else. Retaliation strikes a person the company promised to protect and arrives as an accounting correction. Judith remembers debts perfectly and wrongdoing only when it belongs to another person.

Her voice stays controlled and domestic. Captives are residents, commands are placements, stolen property is relief stock, and coercion is the part of mercy that sentimental people refuse to name. She uses names as receipts: ‘Ansel whom I restored,’ ‘Caldus whose sister I housed,’ ‘Tomas whom I am still willing to forgive.’ Her claim is not innocence. It is that everyone else lacks the nerve to choose who pays. The relief remains real because false usefulness would bind no one.

The clue distribution follows the work. Public machinery leaves many witnesses; exact severance procedures survive in fewer hands and places. Every clue should come from a household, record, victim, route, tool, patron, or worker able to know it. The finale supplies no compensating manual for discoveries missed elsewhere.

Judith has one body and bounded information. Track where she goes after the gallows. Roads, valid Guest crossings, and complete reflected routes can move her. Crows, borrowed voices, commanded guards, hearthlings, the Glass Nurse, and patron manifestations carry intention without duplicating her. Between substantial company operations, spend at most one major response through one surviving channel and leave its receipt: soot, paper, silver scoring, a returning symptom, a courier, a moved wagon, or a witnessed handoff.

The opening begins shortly after dawn, and midnight is a working deadline. One company cannot personally complete ten large operations in sequence. Once procedure, materials, witnesses, care, and authority are established, named local crews may continue persistent work while the company moves to the next critical decision. Record who was entrusted, what remains incomplete, and which routes carry reports. Parallel labor never becomes automatic success, and travel never empties an encounter offstage. At midnight, advance the Underhall to the components actually assembled.

Keep knowledge, access, readiness, care, pact work, feast machinery, and Judith's control separate. Copied evidence remains copied. An opened door remains open. A body honestly buried does not return to the Worm. A restored name stays restored. Direct assault can win rescues, records, routes, or component losses early; it cannot perform a remote severance or conjure the people and materials that work requires.

encounters.title: Saint Orra's Gallows
encounters.summary: Judith places Mara's torch in Tomas's hands, making an illegal execution a public receipt for obedience.
encounters.opening_view: First-light rain has blackened Saint Orra's green. Mara Sedge names her missing daughter from the pyre while her eleven-year-old son grips an unlit torch. Brother Caldus holds a death roll whose cut edge has been rebound; Reeve Pell hides a blackthorn token beneath his coat. Judith Crowl waits under a dry black umbrella. “Tomas,” she says, “a good son proves his innocence by burning the witch who bore him.” One guard lowers her spear. Captain Cleft says, “Three.”
encounters.content:
## The immediate wrong

Mara Sedge has been condemned without a lawful witness. Her thirteen-year-old daughter Nell vanished from the family croft three nights ago. Mara named Judith Crowl as the taker. Before the hour turned, Judith had produced a blackthorn poppet from Mara's chimney, supplied an emergency ordinance, and given Reeve Ansel Pell the courage to sign what she had already decided.

Now Judith has placed the torch in the hands of Mara's eleven-year-old son, Tomas. If he lights the pyre, she promises to receive him and seven-year-old Pate into Saint Mercy House instead of examining them as a witch's accomplices. The bargain kills more than Mara. It makes Tomas carry the act, teaches Pate what refusal costs, and gives the crowd a child whose obedience can be called consent.

## Why the commission reaches the pyre

Ysra's original writ predates Mara's arrest. Duplicate burial fees, missing graves, and two returned Mercy House letters had already caused the canon to send examiners into the vale. After Nell vanished and Mara named Judith, Brother Caldus sent a short addendum by a parish rider who met the commission before dawn. Judith's crow route intercepted enough of the first writ to know the expected day of arrival, but not which road the examiners would use. She therefore denied Mara the customary answer-night and moved the burning to first light. Their arrival before Tomas raises the torch is the consequence of two competing courier networks, not chance.

The commission reaches the green under the original inspection writ and Caldus's addendum. The seal neither dismisses the reeve nor commands his guards; it demands the docket, names witnesses, preserves evidence, and holds Mara alive while the charge is reviewed. Judith expected scrutiny after the ash cooled. She did not expect a rider to put the examiners on the correct road before dawn.
## The execution clock

Run the opening in visible steps rather than resolving it with one check.

1. **The oath.** Beadle Odo Vane reads the charge and makes the crowd repeat that every household “receives mercy and its mistress.”
2. **The torch.** Captain Varro Cleft gives Tomas the torch. Tomas does not move until Judith names Pate.
3. **The challenge.** Present the commission, accuse Judith, question the process, interfere physically, address the crowd, or pretend to cooperate.
4. **The first order.** Judith tells Pell to proceed, orders a marked guard to seize one examiner, or offers a public bargain.
5. **The break.** If resistance holds for even a few moments, Mara or Brother Caldus can put a concrete irregularity before the crowd. Judith must then retreat, escalate openly, or risk losing her appearance of lawful calm.

Questions do not shorten the count. Judith wants witnesses to see Tomas obey, so she leaves enough silence for the boy's choice to become public—and enough time for the examiners to act.

## The legal fault

The emergency conviction fails Blackbriar's own parish custom in four ways:

- no sworn accuser names an act they personally witnessed;
- the poppet was produced by Judith rather than found by the reeve or parish clerk;
- Mara was denied the customary night to answer a capital charge;
- no record explains why Nell Sedge is absent or who holds custody of her.

Canon Ysra's seal authorizes a temporary stay while those defects are examined. Pell knows this. Odo Vane insists that famine ordinances let the reeve ignore it; the cited ordinance concerns spoiled grain, not witchcraft. Put the docket in Caldus's hands and he can expose the substitution before the crowd.

## The commission and later authority

The writ permits four things at the opening: inspect parish and charitable records, preserve evidence, suspend this execution while defects are reviewed, and protect named witnesses from immediate seizure. It does not transfer civil rule, command every guard, authorize unrestricted searches, or make the commission owner of Judith's stores and estate.

Practical authority may broaden only when the fiction supplies a new basis. A discovered unlawful detention supports immediate rescue. A household may invite protection and revoke its own carriers. Pell may issue limited guard-release, evidence-preservation, or evacuation orders in public. Caldus and chapel witnesses may commission the bell and counter-rites. Violence by Judith's people supports ordinary defense and detention. None of those bases authorizes permanent government, secret punishment, or final disposition of property and children. Record which person or institution accepts responsibility for every expansion.

## People on the green

- **Mara Sedge** is burned, exhausted, and exact. She names children, dates, remedies, and the point at which an officer's story changes. She will not ask Judith for mercy. “My Nell is thirteen. She was taken on the ninth night after first frost. Put that in your book before you call her gone.”
- **Tomas Sedge** is eleven and has no patience for an adult's moral summary. He wants to know where Pate is, whether Mara can breathe, and who will stop Cleft if he drops the torch. Give him one credible adult action and he acts at once.
- **Judith Crowl** speaks at household volume. She uses debts as surnames—“Ansel whom I restored,” “Caldus whose sister I housed,” “Tomas whom I am still willing to forgive”—and leaves silence after each one so the crowd must either accept the account or break it aloud.
- **Reeve Ansel Pell** hides decisions inside passive grammar: the charge “was brought,” the ordinance “was found,” the child “has been asked.” Judith cured his wasting sickness by moving it into Elian Darr, and Pell signed the first seizure order afterward. He wants a lawful reason to stop. He also wants someone else to be the person who stopped.
- **Brother Caldus Merrow** remembers missing pages by date, ink, and burial fee. Judith threatened his widowed sister Adela and her son Lark until he concealed discrepancies. Under protection, he can name the substituted leaves and the day the Chapel of the Free Witness was closed.
- **Beadle Odo Vane** prefers offices to people: accused, dependent, household, beneficiary. He drafted the emergency charge knowing the famine ordinance did not authorize it. His daughter received a Mercy House place, and he has chosen repeated cruelty to preserve that advantage.
- **Captain Varro Cleft** speaks in distances and commands. He enjoys the moment when a lawful phrase gives him permission to hurt someone. If Judith leaves, he is the person most likely to continue the burning because the crowd has already been arranged for it.
- **The marked guards**—Edrin Bale, Samet Kett, Will Noll, and Piers Vey—carry tokens or signed cure receipts. Written names can force their bodies, but command arrives visibly: teeth lock, eyes gray, and the mark heats before movement.
- **The unmarked guards**, Cora Pike and Hen Joss, are paid retainers rather than enthralled servants. They can refuse Cleft once the commission is public and the crowd stops lending silence.

## The crowd is not one thing

Use four visible groups.

- **Sedge patients** remember births Mara attended without payment. They will not begin a fight, but two will cut ropes or carry Mara if someone else breaks the first line.
- **Mercy households** owe Judith food, medicine, fuel, or custody. Some defend her sincerely because the aid was real. They become uncertain when asked whether aid authorized Tomas's punishment.
- **The prosecuted families** stand at the edges: Darr, Rusk, Mett, Vey, and Fen households. They possess fragments of older cases and are watching to see whether any challenger survives public speech.
- **Judith's dependents** include paid servants, token-bearing patients, and people with children in Saint Mercy House. They repeat her accusations quickly because they fear what silence will cost.

A crowd response should follow a witnessed act. One villager speaking does not create a mob; one villager speaking and remaining protected makes a second speaker possible.

## Evidence present on the green

The green yields evidence before anyone leaves.

- Mara can direct them to the packets beneath her floor and accuse Saint Mercy House.
- The trial docket shows the false ordinance and Blackbriar Hall as recipient of seized property.
- Caldus can name the old chapel bell and the burial discrepancy.
- The poppet uses Blackbriar petition paper, though the clove-waxed thread is easier to identify at the croft.
- Pell's blackthorn token warms when Judith crosses the courthouse threshold without a spoken invitation.
- Judith's retreat through hearth ash leaves inward-bending flame and warm soot.
- Quill and the other crows depart toward Crow Wood carrying red prisoner-wagon cloth.
- A commanded guard continues speaking in Judith's voice after she has crossed the green.

Award observed facts immediately. Their implications can wait until someone investigates them.

## Ways to stop the burning

### Invoke the commission

Reading the seal aloud and naming one procedural defect forces Pell to acknowledge a stay unless Judith openly overrules him. Mara then needs a custodian and a protected destination. Pell's gaol leaves her within reach of the reeve's token.

### Separate Tomas from the torch

A character can reach Tomas, block Cleft, soak or seize the torch, or give the boy a believable place for Pate and Mara. Tomas is not a test of persuasion skill; he is a child being threatened. Remove the immediate threat or accept the danger of rescuing him physically.

### Turn the process against Judith

Questioning Caldus, examining the poppet, or forcing Odo to cite the ordinance can expose a lie before the whole green. Judith answers with a counteraccusation and an offer: surrender Mara to Saint Mercy House and the burning stops. Acceptance saves Mara now but places her inside Judith's strongest institution.

### Use force

Violence can rescue Mara. Distinguish Judith, Cleft, the four commanded guards, the two ordinary guards, and the crowd. Initiative grants Judith no free massacre. If she loses the green, she retreats through ash and sends retainers after the rescuers.

## Failure forward

If the execution stops only at a cost, choose the smallest consequence that follows.

- Tomas drops the torch after the pyre catches, leaving Mara burned and in urgent need of care.
- Cleft wounds or arrests one rescuer while Mara is cut free by someone else.
- Pell grants a stay but orders Mara confined in an unsafe location.
- Judith escapes with the poppet or docket while Mara is carried clear.
- The crowd accepts Judith's accusation that the examiners endangered children, making Saint Mercy House harder to inspect openly.
- Mara dies only after a meaningful chance to reach her. Her directions survive through Tomas, Caldus, and the croft, but the village loses its strongest living accuser.

## Public result

Record the strongest witnessed refusal, not a numerical morale score.

- **Silence broken:** someone publicly contradicts Judith and survives the scene.
- **Authority contested:** Pell recognizes the stay, a guard refuses Cleft, or the false ordinance is exposed.
- **A witness protected:** Mara, Tomas, Caldus, or another speaker leaves under credible protection.
- **A household commits:** a named household offers food, shelter, transport, testimony, or public revocation.

These commitments determine what villagers will risk later. Judith may punish a person or break a refuge, but she cannot make the crowd forget that resistance occurred.

## Judith's first retaliation

Once the stay is invoked or Mara is removed from the pyre, Judith sends Odo the altered Renewal schedule and commits the feast clock. That ordinary order starts preparations below Blackbriar Hall; it does not grant her an extra remote attack. She then chooses one response supported by a channel she still possesses.

1. She names the examiners as paid witch-finders who manufacture guilt for coin and has Odo post the accusation.
2. She orders Saint Mercy House sealed because outsiders have threatened the children.
3. She sends Quill and three hearthlings to the Sedge Croft to destroy Mara's notes and seize Tomas.
4. She transfers Pell's old sickness back into him and blames the stay.
5. She commands one marked guard to accuse the examiners of bewitchment while the guard's unmarked comrades watch the possession begin.

Every retaliation reveals method. Judith turns dependency, gratitude, or duty into evidence against the victim.

## Leaving the green

Possible departures include Mara under temporary ecclesiastical custody, Tomas as a protected witness, the reeve's records in examiner hands, or flight after a violent rescue. Name every vulnerable person's destination, escort, food, care, and any token, name, gift, or hearth ash Judith owns there.

Unless she is physically restrained, Judith leaves the green for Blackbriar Hall by carriage after the public break. If she instead uses a hearth or reflected route, show the valid carrier, name the destination, and move her one body there. Do not place her at Saint Mercy House and Blackbriar Hall at the same time.

Whatever the route, the village has seen someone refuse Judith publicly. Fear remains, but her claim that resistance is impossible has been broken once.

## Route branches from the green

The opening does not prescribe a visit to the Croft before every other response. Once the immediate burning is resolved, five actionable branches are visible.

- **Sedge Croft:** Mara, Tomas, Quill's flight, the clove-waxed poppet, and the stolen hearth ash point toward the family evidence and refuge problem.
- **Saint Mercy House:** Nell's disappearance, Judith's custody threat, and the promise made to Tomas point directly toward the children and dependent residents.
- **Blackbriar Hall:** the trial docket names the estate as recipient of seized property, and Judith's own departure or servants provide a route for direct confrontation.
- **Chapel of the Free Witness:** Caldus, the false ordinance, and the burial discrepancy point toward the closed parish protections and truthful bell.
- **Crow Wood:** Quill, the red prisoner-wagon cloth, and marked guards point toward the moving captive and familiar network.

Record the first destination, every vulnerable person sent elsewhere, and Judith's last confirmed physical location. One chosen branch gives her time to spend a surviving channel against another. The unchosen encounters remain occupied and active.

encounters.title: Sedge Croft
encounters.summary: Quill and three hearthlings tear through Mara's stripped house while seven case packets, Nell's route, and two planted witnesses remain inside.
encounters.opening_view: Rain blows through Sedge Croft's open door. Quill, a crow with a finger-bone tongue, tears the blue-thread index from Mara's case packets while three soot-thin hearthlings divide the house: chimney, children's beds, root cellar. Someone below pounds twice and chokes. Nell's route map lies beneath a wet black footprint. Quill frees the strip bearing her name and hops toward the fire. Behind it, the cellar latch lifts once.
encounters.content:
## The Sedge household

Mara Sedge is thirty-eight, a midwife who records births by mother, witness, hour, and complication because memory becomes generous after danger passes. Her children are Nell, thirteen; Tomas, eleven; and Pate, seven. Pate begins the adventure hidden at Adela Merrow's cottage. Nell vanished through the hearth after accepting a blackthorn horse Judith sent as a winter gift. Mara saw the child's shadow bend toward the flame before her body followed.

For two nights Mara laid seven prosecutions side by side: each missing dependent, each convenient symptom, each poppet or confession, each grave that never reached the chapel yard. She marked dates in red thread and names in birthing blue. Judith's people came for her before she could carry the comparison to Canon Ysra.

The croft lies below a wet alder bank half a mile from the gallows. It has a kitchen, workroom, two sleeping rooms, root cellar, byre, and one yard gate that can be watched from both pear trees. Ten people can sleep here without crowding. Sixteen can endure one night if the byre is cleared. The pantry will feed the Sedge family for twelve days; every additional mouth turns refuge into an obligation someone must provision.
## Arrival under attack

Quill reached the croft first. The crow, fitted with a human finger-bone for a tongue, tears names from Mara's notes and feeds them into the chimney. Three soot-thin **hearthlings** search the bedrooms for the blackthorn horse. Captain Cleft left two coerced villagers in the root cellar after forcing them to plant the poppet.

Run the intrusion as a short clock.

1. Quill tears the index from one case packet.
2. A hearthling finds Nell's map but cannot interpret it.
3. The chimney fire carries one written name to Blackbriar Hall.
4. The hearthlings seize Tomas or Pate if either child is present.
5. Quill withdraws toward Crow Wood when seriously threatened.

The intruders fight only long enough to destroy evidence or seize a named person. Captive Quill is a vicious but knowledgeable witness. Dead, it leaves a bone tongue that repeats the last three names Judith ordered it to carry.

## People at the croft

- **Mara Sedge**, if alive and free, wants Nell found before she wants Judith exposed. She will cooperate with a larger plan only if it includes a real destination and guard for Tomas and Pate.
- **Tomas Sedge** knows where Nell hid drawings and which crow watched the chimney. He wants to help and will take reckless risks if adults discuss him as cargo.
- **Pate Sedge** may arrive from Adela Merrow's cottage after the gallows. He remembers that the blackthorn horse spoke in Nell's voice one night before she vanished.
- **Sila Darr**, twenty-four, is conscious in the root cellar. Cleft threatened her younger sister Sella at Saint Mercy House until Sila placed the poppet. She can identify Cleft, Odo Vane, and the Blackbriar petition form used to make it.
- **Iven Rusk**, fifty-six, is the other cellar prisoner. Judith has partly removed his name. He remembers facts but cannot say “I,” “me,” or his own name without choking. He knows that his son Jo was moved from Saint Mercy House in a red-curtained wagon.
- **Adela Merrow**, Caldus's widowed sister, can bring Pate, food, bedding, and a cart if the route is secure. Her son Lark is one of the seven name-captives, so she will not accept plans that treat an assault on Mercy House as expendable chaos.

Each witness protects something beyond the case. Sila may prioritize Sella over public testimony. Iven may refuse to be exhibited while nameless. Mara may burn a packet if preserving it would expose a child.

## The rooms

### Kitchen and hearth

The hearth contains no natural ash. A faint ring of hot gray powder surrounds the interior lintel: one of Judith's traveling marks. The blackthorn horse lies split beneath a loose flagstone. Its hollow body contains a curl of paper bearing Nell's full baptismal name in Judith's hand.

Breaking the toy without first removing the paper causes Nell to feel the injury at Mercy House. Burning the paper sends a warning through every linked gift. Washing the name in running water, enclosing it in clean wax, or carrying the whole toy without accepting it as a gift prevents immediate use.

The croft's own ash was taken in a small brass warming pan three nights ago. Replacing it with ash from a freely shared fire and withdrawing Judith's welcome blocks her direct hearth passage here. The old ash must still be found or rendered useless elsewhere.

### Mara's workroom

Mara organized her evidence by families rather than theories. Seven packets compare a Judith gift, a later accusation, a disappearance or illness, and a transfer into Saint Mercy House.

1. **Auda Vey**, keeper of the Chapel of the Free Witness, was accused after its bell broke a commanded man's trance. She died in Pell's gaol; the chapel was closed.
2. **Elian Darr**, tenant farmer, received Pell's wasting sickness after Judith's cure. He was convicted of blighting the reeve and died under restraint. Pell seized the Darr lease for Blackbriar Hall.
3. **Dena Moor**, charcoal burner, reported children at the upper Mercy House windows. A poppet was found in her kiln. She escaped into the western coppice and remains a possible witness.
4. **Bram Kett**, parish gravedigger, recorded burial fees for bodies he never handled. He disappeared on the road to the old orchard. Judith claimed he fled with parish silver.
5. **Ilyra Fen**, laundress and mother of Amey, challenged a cure that moved fever between beds. She was burned after Odo produced a petition-paper poppet. Amey entered Saint Mercy House the same day.
6. **Toman Rusk**, cooper and father of Jo, confessed to cursing Judith after she threatened both his children. He died in a red-curtained prisoner wagon in Crow Wood.
7. **Mara Sedge** accused Judith after Nell vanished. Her case repeats the old sequence quickly enough that Mara recognized it before Judith completed the seizure.

The pattern is not perfectly uniform. Judith has several kinds of mark and sometimes uses ordinary coercion instead of magic. The packets support comparison; they are not a single master proof.

A hidden board contains Mara's most dangerous conclusion: Judith was present at the famine refuge fire, the pox burials, and the first Mercy House naming ceremony fifteen years ago. These are not three local legends. They are three transactions.

### Nell's room

Nell scratched a map beneath her bed after dreaming of the other taken children. The map shows a long house, a room of hanging mirrors, and crows flying toward a wood where the sun appears in the wrong place. Her window sill bears white lime under the black feathers.

Nell also kept a list of seven children who sometimes answered in voices not their own: Nell Sedge, Amey Fen, Jo Rusk, Lark Merrow, Perrin Mett, Sella Darr, and Corin Pike. The list does not say where all seven are now. It establishes that they know one another and have been moved through the same naming system.

### Root cellar

Sila and Iven are bound behind stacked turnip bins. The cellar door carries a Blackthorn Men seizure tag stating that the contents are “contaminated evidence.” The tag grants Judith's marked servants permission to enter if the household accepts the seizure as lawful. Tearing it down is necessary but not sufficient; someone of the household must reject the seizure aloud.

Sila can testify immediately, but moving her sister is her condition for public accusation. Iven's partial naming makes him vulnerable to mirrors and written questions. He can communicate safely by choosing objects, drawing routes, or having another person repeat words he confirms.

### Byre and yard

Two sets of wheel ruts cross the yard: the reeve's seizure cart and a narrower red-curtained wagon from Crow Wood. A loosened byre board creates a route to the alder bank that can move people unseen one at a time. It cannot evacuate a crowd quickly.

## Evidence under pressure

Do not require one exhaustive search. The hearth mark, gift-name, family packets, cellar witnesses, Nell's map, Quill, lime, and wagon tracks all point outward independently. Weak or rushed investigation can preserve some evidence while losing other pieces.

When evidence is threatened, force a priority. A person, packet, familiar, marked gift, and burning room cannot all be secured by one vague action. Losing a document does not erase what a living witness already knows.

## Revoking Judith's welcome

Revocation is a material household act, not a password.

1. **Name the claim.** Identify the token, signature, gift, seizure tag, stolen ash, or person through which Judith asserts welcome.
2. **Withdraw consent.** Each present resident withdraws their own welcome. A child may revoke a gift accepted in their name. No householder may silently speak for an unwilling resident.
3. **Remove the carrier.** Take down tokens and tags, isolate gifts, and clear marked ash without feeding it into another household fire.
4. **Restore the hearth.** Place ash or flame freely shared by someone who understands the use and demands no claim in return.
5. **Witness the act.** One independent witness records who revoked what. Public revocation before midnight also removes the household from the Renewal oath; private revocation blocks direct entry but leaves Judith room to lie about the record.

A suitable declaration is: “No gift purchased this door. Judith Crowl and every claim carried by her token, ash, writing, or servant are refused here.” Exact wording is not required. Intent, authority over one's own welcome, and the physical carriers matter.

At the Sedge Croft, successful revocation produces an immediate sign. The lintel cools, the fire bends outward, and Judith cannot cross directly even if the Sedge names remain in the Mercy Book. She may still send crows, commanded people, smoke, legal officers, or violence from outside.

## Making a refuge

A defended threshold becomes a safehouse only after five decisions:

- who stays and who moves;
- who watches the yard, roof, and hearth;
- which gifts and written names are isolated;
- where food, water, medicine, bedding, and waste go;
- how witnesses give testimony without all occupying one target;
- how a messenger reaches Caldus, Adela, the chapel, or another household; and
- what happens if Judith attacks through law rather than magic.

The croft can become the first public proof that revocation works. It can also become a trap if every witness, child, and packet is concentrated behind one door.

## Judith's attacks on the croft

For each major period spent here, choose one attack through a channel Judith still possesses.

- **Ash passage:** Judith or a hearthling attempts to use the stolen Sedge ash. This fails after proper revocation but reveals where the old ash has been carried.
- **Commanded entry:** a marked guard or frightened neighbor asks for shelter while carrying a concealed token or written name.
- **Legal seizure:** Odo Vane arrives with a warrant naming the croft, residents, and evidence as parish property.
- **Transferred harm:** Pell's illness, a child's fever, or a guard's wound appears in someone placed under protection.
- **Crow fire:** Quill drops a coal wrapped in a copied petition page onto the thatch while another familiar attacks the evidence route.
- **Public accusation:** Judith gathers Mercy households outside and claims the examiners have abducted children and nameless patients.

Every attack creates a choice among people, evidence, secrecy, and public standing. A properly secured refuge never fails by declaration alone.

## Leaving the croft

Before moving on, record:

- Mara's state and chosen priority;
- the location and consent of Tomas and Pate;
- whether Sila and Iven are protected, moved, or willing to testify;
- which of the seven packets survive and who copied them;
- the condition of Nell's name vessel and map;
- whether Quill lives, dies, escapes, or has been redirected;
- whether the Sedge threshold is privately or publicly revoked; and
- what Judith learned through the intrusion.

The croft does not need to become headquarters. It needs to produce concrete people, evidence, and one tested method of refusing Judith's claim.

## If the croft is reached late

A warned Croft changes one asset at a time.

- Quill may destroy one uncopied note group, carry away one named strip, or mark one witness for seizure.
- Cleft's people may move Sila or Iven, but only through the yard and an actual Crow Wood route. The other witness, the cellar construction, and the seizure tag remain.
- One of Mara's seven packets may be removed or burned. The other packets, household comparisons, and witnesses continue to support the pattern.
- A completed household revocation, copied page, protected witness, or distributed packet does not reset because Judith retaliates.

Name what moved, who carried it, and where it went. Leave a track, order, crow strip, damaged hiding place, or witness to the movement. Late arrival narrows the evidence and creates pursuit; it does not make Judith's fifteen-year system leave no trace.

encounters.title: Saint Mercy House
encounters.summary: Saint Mercy House turns bread, beds, medicines, copied names, and transferred illness into a custody system disguised as charity.
encounters.opening_view: Saint Mercy House is warm enough to steam in the rain. Thirty children sit before untouched bowls; nine adults wait with bottles, crutches, and folded blankets. Sister Harl displays clean public accounts while Tib Wale turns the rear-yard key. Behind the sealed east stair, a girl whispers each visitor's whole name in order. Harl asks who will feed thirty-nine dependents if breakfast becomes an inspection. Two empty crates lined with red cord strike the floor beside the stair.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Saint Mercy House earns Judith more loyalty than any threat. Thirty children eat here. Nine adults depend on its beds. Four paid staff keep the visible institution running. Five captives occupy rooms donors are told do not exist. The bread is fresh, the blankets are dry, and some residents would have died without them. Judith expanded the beds, medicines, and receiving forms because effective care places frightened people inside rooms and records she controls. Rescue can therefore be made to look like theft from the people she selected as witnesses.

Arrival may come under Canon Ysra's seal, as kin or donors, through the laundry drain, behind a rescued witness, or in open force. Every entrance raises three questions:

- Which records, hidden rooms, and name vessels remain reachable before Harl begins moving them?
- Which people require bottles, stretchers, chosen carriers, familiar faces, or protected names before they can cross the door safely?
- Who will receive them, feed them, and answer Judith when she calls the evacuation abandonment or abduction?

A single inspection roll cannot answer all three. Let access, trust, evidence, medical safety, hidden captives, and departure routes change on their own clocks.
## Current occupancy

The visible population consists of thirty children and nine adult dependents. Four paid staff run the house. Five captives are concealed upstairs:

- **Nell Sedge**, thirteen, has counted every mirror and learned the order in which a stolen name must be returned.
- **Amey Fen**, twelve, is forced to answer in dead Ilyra Fen's voice after dusk.
- **Lark Merrow**, nine, is kept near the infirmary so Judith can compel Brother Caldus.
- **Sella Darr**, eight, is held because her sister Sila witnessed the planted poppet.
- **Eda Lorn**, thirty-six, is an infirmary patient whose family was falsely told she recovered and left.

All seven silvered name vessels are still in the mirror dormitory. The bodies of Jo Rusk, Perrin Mett, and Corin Pike are elsewhere, but their written names remain here. Judith can therefore punish or command them at a distance, and their vessels matter before their bodies are found. The Glass Nurse also coordinates seven copied identities through the silver, but vessels alone cannot form the captive choir. Harl's transfer order must bring at least four living, controlled children to the Underhall; securing a vessel neither rescues its owner nor silences that owner's physical voice.

## Principal people

- **Sister Harl**, steward, knowingly collects names, orders punishments, and prepares transfers. She believes dependency should be used without apology. She is culpable, but she has told herself Judith preserves the institution rather than spending it. Proof that the feast will consume residents, combined with a credible evacuation plan, can make her turn on Judith. Mere exposure of abuse makes her defend the house more fiercely.
- **Matron Eda Wren**, day matron, has tolerated coercion because she can point to children who were fed. When immediate harm to a named child is placed before her, she chooses the child. She can organize the visible residents, identify medical needs, and keep a frightened evacuation from becoming a stampede.
- **Ressa Pold**, cook, hides extra bread and has memorized which children cannot return home. She will help quietly before she will testify publicly.
- **Tib Wale**, porter and night guard, accepts Harl's discipline and enjoys deciding who is grateful enough to enter. He controls the front keys and the bell pull to Crow Wood.
- **Old Fen Corren**, resident cobbler, has copied Mercy Book entries into shoe soles. He refuses to leave the infirmary patients behind and knows which service shoes conceal pages.
- **The Glass Nurse**, a joint reflection made from seven stolen names, occupies the mirror dormitory after dark or whenever Harl uncovers the central glass. It imitates desired voices, repeats marked-room conversations, and gives commands that sound like trusted people.

Use four or five resident voices in play rather than presenting the house as a crowd. Good choices include:

- **Henn Lye**, fifteen, who portions food and will organize older children if given an actual destination;
- **Mira Coil**, eleven, who remembers the full names Harl made residents repeat;
- **Bess Orm**, eight, who can distinguish the Glass Nurse because its reflection smiles before the speaker does;
- **Tamsin Pike**, fourteen, who knows Corin was taken across the east bridge and wants the vessel bearing his name protected;
- **Sera Quill**, a blind basketmaker, who can identify Harl and Judith by step and perfume and does not rely on false reflections;
- **Dall Oat**, an adult laborer with transferred lung sickness, who can walk only if his sealed bottle travels with him.

Residents do not become loyal because a door opens. They ask where the youngest will sleep, whether siblings remain together, who carries medicine, whether Judith can enter the destination, and whether their rescuers will return for those still hidden.

## House plan

### 1. Petition hall

A polished public room holds the donor board, intake desk, and six visible gift cabinets. Harl receives inspectors here. The displayed ledger is genuine but incomplete: it records food and beds while omitting transferred illness, hidden custody, and mirror vessels. Tib can lock the outer doors from the desk. A blackthorn lamp above the hearth lets Judith hear formal petitions spoken beneath it.

Reading Canon Ysra's commission publicly opens the refectory, kitchens, visible dormitory, and public accounts. Harl calls the upper east wing unsafe because of roof damage. Pressing that boundary begins the inspection clock.

### 2. Refectory and schoolroom

Thirty children sit in six assigned groups. The arrangement lets staff count absences instantly and makes private conversation difficult. The slate lesson repeats the Renewal phrase: “We receive mercy and its mistress.” Children have altered several letters so the sentence reads differently from the doorway than from the tables.

A resident speaks honestly only after seeing how speech will not punish the next table. Move Harl, Tib, and the blackthorn lamp out of earshot before offering broad promises.

### 3. Kitchen, pantry, and rear yard

Ressa keeps enough food for four ordinary days or one hurried evacuation. The rear gate opens onto the parish granary yard, but Harl has stacked it with winter fuel to make it appear unusable. A thin old wall behind the flour bins can be opened into the granary passage without collapsing the kitchen.

The pantry contains gifts marked for particular households. Removing a gift may block one known channel, but do not treat the pantry as every token in the vale. The inventory is useful for identifying carriers and planning household revocations.

### 4. Cobbler room and laundry drain

Fen's bench contains shoe soles copied from the Mercy Book. The copies are partial but independent of Judith's records. A stone laundry drain runs beneath the old Darr wash channel. Small residents and unarmored adults can crawl it; stretchers and the infirmary bottles cannot.

The drain is the safest covert exit for a few children and the worst route for a mass flight. Sila Darr can receive people at the far end if warned.

### 5. Visible dormitory and roof schoolroom

These rooms are clean, crowded, and genuinely used. The roof schoolroom has a shuttered loading window above a cooper's awning. A rope crossing can move a few able children when the lower floor is controlled, but rain, panic, and the visible drop make it unsuitable for the sick or very young.

A false wall behind the copybooks opens onto the sealed east stair. Nell persuaded Mira and Bess to hide its iron key inside a hollow counting rod.

### 6. Records room

The records room contains the **Mercy Book**, token lists, donor correspondence, altered admission dates, infirmary transfers, and Sister Harl's feast checklist. The shelves are arranged so that removing the central book releases a blackthorn catch and rings the Crow Wood bell unless the side weights are replaced.

The clue-bearing evidence is distributed rather than bundled into one confession:

- admission and trial dates expose Judith's manufactured prosecutions;
- gift columns connect accepted aid to later access incidents;
- token lists identify specific household carriers;
- the feast checklist names the Mercy Book, hearth tokens, and seven stolen-name voices;
- Harl's sealed transfer order sends captives and vessels through Crow Wood if the upper floor is breached.

Copying, dividing, or publicly reading records may be more useful than carrying one vulnerable book. The Mercy Book itself remains a component of the final rite.

### 7. Punishment passage

Four narrow closets have no interior handles. The walls contain written names beneath limewash. Speaking a captive's name in the passage makes the matching door seem to move farther away. Scraping away one inscription gives that person a brief interval in which Judith cannot stop them at a marked threshold, but it also alerts the Glass Nurse.

The closets preserve immediate evidence of abuse: fingernail dates, punishment tallies, and phrases residents were forced to copy. They do not replace the broader records needed to establish the system.

### 8. Mirror dormitory

Seven narrow mirrors hang from blackthorn frames. Each silvered name vessel is a folded slip sealed between the backing and the glass. The central mirror has no independent vessel; it combines the seven reflections into the Glass Nurse.

The Nurse first uses comfort. It speaks in Mara's voice to Nell, Ilyra's voice to Amey, or one examiner's own voice to another company member. It can then:

- repeat a command through a voice Judith has borrowed;
- show a false ally opening the wrong door;
- report speech from a marked household;
- hold one named child at a threshold;
- inflict sharp pain when Harl scores the matching vessel.

The Nurse cannot invent knowledge absent from Judith's channels. It repeats overheard speech, recorded names, resident memories, and personal information given through accepted gifts. Covering the central glass with dull cloth prevents it from coordinating the seven vessels, though individual bonds remain.

### 9. Suspended infirmary

Five patients lie in a warm locked room above the kitchen flue. Judith has transferred illnesses from paying households into dependent bodies, then drawn the worst symptoms into sealed glass bottles so the recipients remain alive enough to serve. Each chain consists of a payer entry, a recipient entry, a wax-sealed bottle, and the living patient. The treatment is not a cure.

Current patients include Eda Lorn; Dall Oat, carrying a brewer's lung sickness; Ysa Bell, carrying seizures removed from a magistrate's niece; Marric Soil, carrying a wasting fever; and Noma Feld, carrying the recurring chills of a Blackbriar tenant.

Do not smash or casually open the bottles. Heat, breakage, or separation from the matching patient releases stored symptoms into the patient or the nearest breathing body. Safe movement requires keeping each bottle upright, cool, labeled, and beside its recipient. The hidden infirmary book identifies failed transfers sent to the White Pits and restores eleven erased identities.

Medical rescue is possible without solving the Worm pact. It requires stretchers, blankets, clean water, receiving beds, and people willing to care for contagious-looking patients whom Judith has publicly described as cursed.

### 10. East bridge and transfer cabinet

A covered bridge joins the upper floor to an old service tunnel leading toward Crow Wood and Blackbriar Hall. The transfer cabinet holds red cords, covered mirror crates, prisoner hoods, and Harl's emergency order. A pull-bell summons Garran Pike's wagon.

This is Judith's extraction route, not a convenient secret exit. Seizing it can intercept the wagon, rescue transferred captives, or send false instructions. Failing to control it gives Harl a concrete way to move vessels and children rather than allowing captives to vanish arbitrarily.

## The inspection clock

Advance the clock for prolonged delay, a loud accusation with open exits, the record-room catch, or unrestricted staff messages. Careful questions consume table time, not fictional minutes by themselves.

1. **Polite containment.** Harl produces public accounts and separates inspectors from residents.
2. **Quiet preparation.** Tib bars the rear yard; Eda Wren is ordered to assemble visible children for a “health count.”
3. **Records move.** Harl sends the feast checklist and several token pages toward the east bridge.
4. **Captives move.** Nell, Amey, Lark, and Sella are hooded; the seven vessels are packed into two crates.
5. **The wagon answers.** Garran's people enter the service tunnel. If the route is blocked, Harl prepares the roof and front-door alternatives instead.
6. **Judith intervenes.** Judith arrives through the petition-hall hearth or a mirror if the relevant pact remains intact and she is not already committed at another site.

Every step leaves something actionable. A moved ledger creates a courier to follow. Hooded captives can resist, leave marks, or delay staff. The arriving wagon exposes Crow Wood. Judith's entrance reveals a channel and places her in reach.

## Approaches

### Inspection under commission

Harl obeys the letter of the commission while narrowing every request. She offers clean rooms, real food stores, and selected residents who will truthfully say they were helped. Compare records, separate staff, test the sealed wing, and ask residents about absences; a demanded confession only strengthens her posture.

A lawful inspection provides the best public evidence and the slowest access. It becomes much stronger if Mara, Caldus, Sila, or another protected witness is present.

### Donor, applicant, or kin entry

A false donor can reach the gift cabinets and petition process. A claimed relative must answer details Harl can compare to the Mercy Book. An applicant is offered food or lodging and asked to sign. Accepting is a real choice: Judith gains a channel only through an explicitly named gift and carrier; ordinary hospitality does not acquire a hidden cost after the fact.

Residents judge visitors by practical commitments. A believable rescue conversation names beds, guardians, food, transport, and how siblings stay together.

### Covert entry

The laundry drain reaches Fen's room. The granary passage reaches the kitchen. The roof reaches the schoolroom. Covert movement can bypass the public shield but creates a harder problem once people must leave. Infiltrators who secure records and routes before revealing themselves give Eda Wren and residents something around which to organize.

### Assault

The front hall makes violence look like an attack on children. Tib locks doors, Harl places visible residents between armed intruders and the stairs, and the Glass Nurse imitates company voices. Control of hearth, bell, and exits can make a direct assault succeed, but residents, records, and routes bear separate consequences.

If the Guest in Ash pact is intact, Judith can turn the petition hearth inward or move through it. If the Worm pact is intact, she can force one stored symptom into a nearby body. If the Child pact is intact, she can command through a vessel or false reflection. A weakened or severed pact removes that response visibly.

## Name-vessel handling

The seven vessels are evidence, hostages, and people’s stolen property. Treat each one separately.

1. Cover the mirror with dull, unpatterned cloth before opening the frame.
2. Do not read the written name aloud in a reflected room.
3. Keep each vessel with a free carrier who is not acting under Judith's written command.
4. Mark which body is present, missing, or already located elsewhere.
5. Do not break the vessel before the owner or a free witness returns the name in an unborrowed reflection.

Covering a vessel blocks sight and coordinated use. It does not return the name. Scratching or breaking it early causes pain, disorientation, loss of voice, or impaired recognition in the owner; it does not provide a clean shortcut. Nell knows the correct sequence because she witnessed two earlier failed attempts.

Bodies can be rescued now and vessels carried toward Moonless Mere later. Jo, Perrin, and Corin's vessels may be secured while their absent bodies remain unresolved.

## Evacuation procedure

Before the first large movement, establish four facts:

- a receiving place for children who cannot safely return home;
- a medically suitable destination for infirmary patients;
- a protected carrier and route for each name vessel and copied record;
- an accountable adult for every group leaving the house.

Then move in priorities rather than one undifferentiated crowd:

1. prevent transfer of hidden captives and vessels;
2. stabilize infirmary patients and pair each with the correct bottle;
3. move the youngest children and anyone Judith can command directly;
4. move witnesses and records through different routes where possible;
5. move remaining residents with food, blankets, and named receiving households.

Available exits:

- **Front court:** highest capacity and best for public legitimacy; unsafe while Tib, Cleft, or Judith controls the crowd.
- **Granary passage:** accepts stretchers and supply carts once the flour-bin wall is opened; leads to parish ground and can support the infirmary evacuation.
- **Laundry drain:** discreet and defensible for six small or able people at a time; cannot take stretchers, bottles in cases, or a panicked mass.
- **Roof schoolroom:** useful for a few trapped children when lower floors are lost; slow and hazardous in rain.
- **East bridge:** quickest route for the vessel crates but leads into Judith's prisoner network. Use it after seizing the tunnel, intercepting the wagon, or deliberately setting a pursuit.

A disorderly rescue still saves people. Record who escaped, who remained, which route Judith now knows, what evidence was secured, and which dependents lack a safe destination. Do not erase progress because the evacuation was imperfect.

## Sister Harl's decisions

Sister Harl has spent years turning people into beds, bottles, meal places, and transfer lines. She is neither a secret rebel nor a zealot eager to die for Judith. She tells herself that someone must keep the institution functioning and has let “functioning” excuse punishments, hidden rooms, stolen names, and patients stored as liabilities.

Calling her a hypocrite does not move her. Three concrete facts can:

- the feast list identifies named residents as voices to be spent, not people to be housed;
- the rescuers can show where the hidden residents will sleep, who carries each bottle, and who answers for the next meal;
- Judith orders her to sacrifice one person Harl has personally kept alive.

Before that break, Harl delays by count and category. She narrows answers, moves records, threatens to divide kin, and deploys the Glass Nurse while insisting that disorder is the greater cruelty. If she turns, she gives up the record-room weights, calls Eda Wren by name instead of title, opens the flour-bin route, and holds the east bridge for one evacuation wave.

Her help does not acquit her. Survivors may still charge her for transfers, punishments, and name custody she knowingly administered. If she escapes, she carries either the feast checklist or one vessel crate—never the entire encounter's evidence—and leaves a route that can be pursued.

## Judith's response

Judith prefers to arrive after care has been promised. She walks the receiving plan line by line and points to every empty space.

Under inspection, she admits the bread, beds, medicine, and forms, then requires proof for each concealed abuse. Under infiltration, she names the trespass and offers one examiner a tailored benefit for leaving the upper floor closed. Under assault, she spends the narrowest surviving pact channel and retreats only after rescuers remove something she cannot rename as temporary confusion.

During public exposure, Judith does not say Saint Mercy House is harmless. She asks who feeds thirty children tomorrow, which cottage accepts a fever patient, and whose winter grain the rescuers have volunteered. Then she punishes the first person who answers: a vessel scores until a child recants, a stored symptom returns to that speaker's favored household, or a marked guardian reaches for their own dependent. Exposure does not invite confession or reform. It tells Judith which relationship to turn into the next correction.

Her claim is always the same: mercy consists of choosing who pays, and only she has the honesty to keep the account. Her answer is the person she hurts. Judith created the scarcity, concealed the alternatives, and calls ownership the price of solving what she arranged.

She can leave through the petition hearth while the Guest channel survives, through prepared glass while the Child channel survives, or over the east bridge if her body can reach it. She cannot answer a simultaneous crisis in person. If another pact site already holds her attention, Harl runs the house and Judith's response arrives through one bounded channel.

## Outcomes to record

At the end of the encounter, record:

- each hidden captive rescued, moved, or left behind;
- the current location and condition of all seven name vessels;
- which infirmary patients and bottles were matched and moved safely;
- whether the Mercy Book, copied pages, token lists, feast checklist, and transfer order were secured, destroyed, moved, or publicly read;
- which staff aided, resisted, fled, or were captured;
- which residents have named receiving households and which remain dependent on improvised refuge;
- whether Judith's public legitimacy strengthened, fractured, or became divided by household;
- which route now points toward Crow Wood, Moonless Mere, the White Pits, the Chapel, or Blackbriar Hall.

A strong result rescues everyone onsite, preserves the vessels, secures distributed evidence, and exposes Judith's machinery. A partial result may save people while losing the Mercy Book, preserve evidence while Harl moves captives, or force a pursuit into Crow Wood. Every result leaves changed lives and actionable routes, never only a solved room.

## If the house is reached late or skipped

Saint Mercy House cannot be emptied offstage by one order.

- One completed transfer wave can move up to four ambulatory captives, one vessel crate, or one matched infirmary patient and bottle through the east bridge. It cannot move all three categories at once.
- Every transfer requires custody papers, staff, the bridge route, and either Garran's wagon or a smaller actual conveyance. Its destination is Crow Wood, Blackbriar Hall, the service route, or the Underhall.
- Thirty visible children, adult dependents, most stores, the suspended infirmary apparatus, and records too bulky for the chosen wave remain available.
- Harl may take the feast checklist or one vessel crate if she flees, never every vessel, patient, and record.
- People already evacuated, vessels already covered or removed, and evidence already copied remain in their recorded states.

If Saint Mercy House remains unvisited until the finale, use the transfer record to determine which stolen-name bodies physically reached choir bays. Populate no bay by assumption. The untransferred residents remain a live rescue, testimony, and care problem above ground.

encounters.title: Blackbriar Hall
encounters.summary: Petitioners queue beside winter stores and confiscated property while Judith's ledgers, couriers, pact records, and stair below remain in active use.
encounters.opening_view: Blackbriar Hall's petition line moves between two desks. Dain Orm weighs grain for a coughing woman; Odo Vane records the sack, the cure, and her son's winter labor in separate columns. Confiscated cradles prop the doors open. Corin Pike crosses the hall with a loose Mercy Book leaf while Captain Cleft seals the private stair. Seven chimneys smoke without fuel. A brass speaking tube clicks below. Odo tears need from debt and sends Corin toward the undercroft.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Blackbriar Hall is a house arranged to make ownership look like administration. Petitioners enter at the front. Confiscated grain, medicine, fuel, tools, and furniture leave through the side court under new labels. Crows and servants deliver names to the ash gallery. Judith's private rooms keep the living copies of her pacts. The undercroft receives prisoners and opens onto the Hollow Feast.

The hall remains usable under Canon Ysra's commission, through the petition line, behind the red-curtained wagon, across a mirror, by the root-cut tunnel, or through a broken gate. Each route exposes a different piece of the same household.

The stores are real and many families need them. Much of the stock was bought with seized property, transferred suffering, coerced work, or debts designed never to close. Fire and indiscriminate looting punish the households before Judith. An inventory, named custody, and public redistribution separate relief from the woman who insists relief proves ownership.

Judith ordinarily remains here until the Renewal nears completion. She may receive the examiners before witnesses, spend one surviving channel to answer trouble elsewhere, descend when the feast has enough components, or leave Odo and Cleft to hold the house while she corrects a public refusal. Mark every departure. Blackbriar Hall is her center, not proof that she occupies every room at once.
## The household

Blackbriar Hall ordinarily contains twenty people before transferred patients, prisoners, or petitioners are counted.

- **Judith Crowl** receives petitioners, chooses punishments, and controls the pact channels that remain intact.
- **Beadle Odo Vane** keeps the legal, seizure, and accusation records. He is a willing collaborator. He bargains when cornered, but his first offer is always someone else's safety.
- **Captain Varro Cleft** commands six Blackthorn guards at the hall and can call eight more from the village. He enjoys turning official language into permission for violence.
- **Steward Dain Orm** runs the charity stores and confiscated-property auctions. He knows the stores are stolen and profits from every shortage. He will flee with portable silver before defending Judith personally.
- **Merrit Coil**, Judith's housekeeper, accepted a cure for her brother and then spent twelve years making rooms ready for threatened guests. She knows the house's ordinary locks and schedules. Her complicity is substantial, but she has never carried a name vessel or knowingly delivered a child.
- **Corin Pike**, fifteen, is called an apprentice and used as a page. He carries separated Mercy Book leaves between the study, petition hall, and Underhall. His own name vessel remains elsewhere, so commands through his written name can turn his route against rescuers.
- **Eda Lorn** begins at Saint Mercy House. If Harl's transfer reaches the hall, Eda is placed in the warm cellar because Judith uses her body to receive illnesses that would otherwise expose the White Pits. Otherwise the cellar contains her prepared bed, labeled lines, and transfer order.
- Eight cooks, porters, cleaners, and clerks work for wages or debt relief. Three have accepted marked gifts, two know Judith is a witch, and none knows the whole machinery.
- Six guards hold the public entrances. Cora Pike or Hen Joss may be among them if prior events have not separated the ordinary guards from Cleft.

Do not make the whole staff fight to the death. Ask what each person knows, has accepted, fears losing, and can physically reach.

## Ways into the hall

### Public petition

The front doors remain open while the Renewal is publicly underway. Petitioners are searched for weapons but not for copied documents, household tokens, or concealed tools. An official commission, a person Judith expects to control, or evidence that can embarrass her in front of petitioners buys time inside.

Public entry places witnesses around Judith. It also gives her the opportunity to offer real relief, expose private facts obtained through her network, and portray any seizure as an attack on food and medicine.

### Formal inspection

A lawful stay from Pell, Canon Ysra's commission, Caldus's burial records, or proof of false seizure can compel Odo to open the petition hall, counting room, and public stores. It does not by itself open Judith's study, the ash gallery, or the undercroft. Every refusal, substituted record, and moved object becomes evidence.

### Service tunnel

The concealed road through Crow Wood enters the receiving cellar below the charity stores. The tunnel is wide enough for one wagon. Its iron gate can be opened from Garran's road key, from Corin's page key, or by forcing the counterweight. A forced gate rings the ash-gallery service bell and advances the hall response, but it does not collapse the tunnel.

### Reflected corridor

While the Child Behind Glass remains active, a known mirror route from Saint Mercy House or Moonless Mere can reach the guest corridor. Covering the arrival mirror prevents immediate pursuit. An unguarded traveler may arrive in a prepared guest room rather than the intended corridor.

### Marked hearth

A person carrying accepted ash or a household token can be drawn through the ash gallery when Judith opens the matching hearth. Deliberately using the channel provides a rapid route but briefly exposes the carrier's household door in the Underhall. A fully revoked household cannot be used this way.

### Assault or siege

The terrace can be climbed, the gates broken, and the hall surrounded. A direct assault makes Judith spend visible channels and may keep her from moving records quietly. It also places petitioners, servants, stores, and captives between intruders and the estate's defenders. Cleft uses that fact deliberately.

## Hall response

Track the hall's response by changed control, not by an abstract alarm that makes every door impossible.

1. **Observe.** Clerks record names, crows leave the roof, and Judith chooses whether to receive the examiners personally.
2. **Separate.** Odo moves petitioners to the stores, Cleft closes the private stair, and Corin is ordered to carry one packet toward the undercroft.
3. **Preserve the machinery.** The Mercy Book or its separated leaves move downward; accusation drafts and the network board remain behind because they are too useful to burn blindly.
4. **Move vulnerable people.** If Eda Lorn has arrived, she is prepared for the service wagon; otherwise an order is sent to bring her from Saint Mercy House. One present captive or servant is moved, and Merrit is ordered to destroy a single named evidence class.
5. **Use an intact pact.** Judith crosses a hearth, transfers a wound, or opens a false corridor. Use only a channel she still possesses and reveal its physical carrier.
6. **Commit to the feast.** Judith descends, Cleft holds the stair or retreats to the thorn court, and Odo begins reading the household names below.

Interrupting a step creates an opportunity. A courier can be followed, a moved captive can be rescued, a selected document can be preserved, and an intact channel can be traced.

## Areas

### 1. Thorn terrace and front doors

Clipped blackthorn hedges form waist-high lanes around the approach. Forty-seven household emblems are cut into the stone curb; each corresponds to a currently displayed token. Eleven blank recesses await households that have signed but not yet displayed one.

The front doors swing inward under the Guest in Ash. If the refuge doors have been opened correctly, soot outlines become visible around the hinges and the doors can no longer close without someone physically moving them. If the Guest is severed, they are ordinary heavy doors.

Petitioners waiting outside can witness official refusals, Judith's admissions, or violence. They are not a passive crowd. Several have come for food that cannot safely be delayed.

### 2. Petition hall

Two desks face each other. At the first, people state what they need. At the second, Odo records what they owe. The room contains cure receipts, custody forms, grain extensions, and gratitude signatures in separate drawers. The separation lets Judith publicly display need while privately joining obligation.

A brass speaking tube reaches the Underhall lectern. During the feast, names read below can be answered or corrected here. A free household representative speaking through the tube can publicly revoke a signature if the relevant page is present or accurately identified.

Judith receives challengers here when she wants witnesses. She does not deny being useful. She asks which patient should lose medicine, which child should lose a bed, and which household should feed a refugee if her stores are seized. The honest answer is a distribution plan, not an argument that the needs are unreal.

### 3. Charity stores

The north rooms hold grain, lamp oil, dried apples, winter blankets, fever bark, bandages, and six locked chests of parish silver. Every stack bears two marks: the household from which it was confiscated or purchased under pressure, and the household promised relief.

Destroying the stores punishes both sets of people. An inventory made with independent witnesses allows the goods to be redistributed without preserving Judith's claim. Dain Orm knows which measures are short, which medicines are genuine, and which casks carry blackthorn splinters.

Three marked gift crates are prepared for the Renewal. Removing their blackthorn linings prevents them from creating new household carriers. Burning them while the Guest remains intact sends their ash to the gallery.

### 4. Counting room and accusation press

Odo's room contains the seizure ledgers, seven old prosecution files, prepared accusations for six future targets, blank confessions, parish seals, and the small press that makes petition-paper poppets.

The prepared cases are not vague threats. Each names an incident Judith intends to create: a mill fever, a chapel fire, a missing infant, spoiled grain, a guard's seizure, and a failed cure. The evidence lists leave spaces for whichever frightened witness can be coerced afterward.

The room also contains Odo's private index of who knows each legal substitution. Seizing the index exposes witnesses to danger unless protection plans exist. Copying and dividing it preserves the pattern without concentrating every name in one vulnerable bundle.

### 5. Public dining room

Judith feeds twelve petitioners here every evening. Three unused chairs stand at the head of the table. Their undersides bear the titles **Guest in Ash**, **Worm in White**, and **Child Behind Glass**, together with dates and payments for each voluntary renewal.

The meals are ordinary and nourishing. Judith uses the room to insist that appetite proves consent to her whole order. A person can eat food without inviting her patrons. Stating and witnessing that distinction weakens her social argument but does not replace physical revocation.

If a pact has been severed, its chair splits along the grain and cannot be repaired. If weakened, the corresponding payment marks blur or bleed their material sign: soot, white moisture, or false silvering.

### 6. Ash gallery

Forty-seven shallow hearths line a long room. Each bears a household name, a sample of stolen hearth ash, and a socket matching a blackthorn token. Eleven additional hearths hold signed paper but no ash. Five cold bays correspond to households that have avoided both.

The gallery is a communications network, not a bank of portals Judith can use without cost.

- A lit hearth lets Judith observe flame and sound in the matching marked home.
- Crossing requires an intact Guest pact, a warm matching token, and enough open floor on both sides for a body.
- Carrying a message requires paper, ash, or a crow. Thoughts do not travel by themselves.
- A privately revoked household causes its hearth to smoke and show no image.
- A publicly witnessed revocation turns the household name outward on its iron label and prevents the Underhall from counting that door in the common welcome.

The **network maintenance board** lists every current carrier: token, ash sample, written name, servant, crow route, and known failure. Removing it does not end the network; it identifies what must be tested and where Judith has already lost access.

Pulling ash samples from the hearths is safe only if they are covered separately. Mixing or burning them while the Guest remains active can create a temporary common passage between households.

### 7. Judith's study

The study contains five crucial records that Judith cannot replace before midnight.

1. **The living false shelter ledger.** Ash restores erased names until it is burned under the proper refuge conditions.
2. **The Mercy Book master index.** It maps every signature to its household, token, dependents, and underhall door. The full ceremonial book may be here, in transit, or already below depending on earlier events.
3. **The three injury ledgers.** They record where Judith sent wounds, illnesses, and reflected harms. Current entries reveal which pact still carries each protection.
4. **The contingency matrix.** It states plainly that the common welcome survives one lost feast component but collapses when any two of the Mercy Book, token network, and captive choir fail.
5. **The accusation drafts.** They establish that Judith planned crimes before their supposed evidence existed.

The desk has no single self-destruct device. Judith values these records and relies on them. If she must destroy something, she chooses one class, uses a specific channel, and leaves the action visible.

A small portrait shows Judith at twenty-three before the first pact. Behind it is her first rejected petition for an ordinary parish office. It explains the injury to her pride; it does not excuse what she chose next.

### 8. Prepared guest rooms

Five rooms contain gifts tailored to common adventuring wants. Choose only those that fit actual characters.

- A military guest finds a restored standard and a written promise that one dead comrade can answer orders again.
- A healer finds a sleeping patient whose illness Judith can remove immediately by naming another recipient.
- A scholar finds an accurate page from a lost work, with the remaining leaves promised after the feast.
- A disgraced or guilty guest finds a confession already signed by someone willing to bear public blame.
- A claimant finds a deed transferring confiscated land and the testimony needed to make it lawful.

The gifts are real enough to tempt. None takes effect without a legible act of acceptance: signing, carrying, naming the beneficiary, drinking, opening the parcel, or inviting Judith to complete it. Examining, refusing, preserving as evidence, or redirecting a gift does not silently bind someone.

The Child Behind Glass can make a room appear to contain a loved or trusted person only through an uncovered mirror and a written name. Covering the mirror leaves the physical gift and removes the false person.

### 9. Servants' passage and page room

Corin Pike sleeps beside shelves of separated Mercy Book leaves. Each leaf contains three to six household entries so no servant carries the whole plan. Corin has hidden copied page numbers under the bed slats and marked every route where Cleft cannot see him.
